sources.title: Age and High-Growth Entrepreneurship (Center for Administrative Records Research and Applications working paper)
sources.measures: the mean age of a person at the moment they founded a United States firm that went on to employ someone, computed from the Census Bureau's Longitudinal Business Database and linked federal earnings and partnership records for firms founded across an eight-year stretch; a working paper by named academic authors and a Census Bureau economist, which states that its opinions and conclusions are the authors' own
sources.excerpt: the mean age for the entrepreneurs at founding is 41.9
sources.notes: The full sentence names the founder count and the years counted; the excerpt is the clause carrying the figure. The same paper reports a higher mean for the fastest-growing ventures, which this record does not claim.

milestones.label: Founding a firm that goes on to employ someone
milestones.population: People who founded a United States firm that went on to employ at least one person, across an eight-year stretch of linked federal business and tax records. The figure is the mean age at the moment of founding across every kind of new firm the records hold, from a restaurant to a software company.
whatChanges: The middle of the age distribution for people who start a firm that goes on to employ someone sits in the early forties rather than in the twenties.
The count covers every kind of new firm in the records and not only the ones that grow quickly; the paper reports an older mean age for those.
It is a mean across a very wide spread, and founders much younger and much older than it are ordinary.
milestones.notes: Authored in the fix pass. Re-authoring the comparison-as-window records removed a cultural expectation whose window had been borrowed from a brokerage's published guideline and stretched across most of adult life, and that borrowed window had been the only thing standing between the early forties and a stretch of years with nothing discrete in them. This is the honest replacement: a measured age that actually falls there, quoted from a fetched page, rather than a wider window on a record that did not earn one.
